metadata.title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization (Loshchilov & Hutter, 2017)
metadata.framework: fixing the interaction between L2 regularization and adaptive learning rates in Adam
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:1711.05101.

nodes.name: L2 regularization vs weight decay: the distinction
nodes.statement: For SGD, L2 regularization ($\nabla_\theta f + \lambda \theta$) and weight decay ($\theta \leftarrow (1 - \lambda')\theta - \alpha \nabla f$) are equivalent with $\lambda' = \alpha \lambda$. For adaptive methods like Adam, they are NOT equivalent: L2 regularization adds $\lambda \theta$ to the gradient, which then gets scaled by $1/\sqrt{\hat{v}_t}$, making the effective regularization per-parameter and dependent on the gradient history. Weight decay subtracts $\lambda' \theta$ directly from $\theta$, independent of the adaptive step.

nodes.name: AdamW update rule (decoupled weight decay)
nodes.statement: AdamW modifies Adam by decoupling weight decay from the gradient-based update: $\theta_t = (1 - \lambda) \theta_{t-1} - \alpha \frac{\hat{m}_t}{\sqrt{\hat{v}_t} + \epsilon}$. Equivalently: compute Adam update from gradient $g_t = \nabla f_t(\theta_{t-1})$ (WITHOUT L2 term), then apply weight decay separately. The weight decay $\lambda$ is independent of the adaptive learning rate.

nodes.name: SGDW (decoupled weight decay for SGD)
nodes.statement: For completeness, SGDW applies the same decoupling to SGD with momentum: $\theta_t = (1 - \lambda)\theta_{t-1} - \alpha \nabla f_t(\theta_{t-1})$. For SGD (without adaptive rates), SGDW and SGD with L2 regularization are equivalent (up to rescaling $\lambda$).

nodes.name: Learning rate and weight decay coupling in Adam
nodes.statement: In standard Adam with L2 regularization, the optimal weight decay $\lambda$ depends on the learning rate $\alpha$, batch size, and training duration. This coupling makes hyperparameter tuning difficult. AdamW decouples these: the optimal weight decay $\lambda$ is largely independent of $\alpha$, enabling separate tuning.

nodes.name: AdamW generalizes better than Adam+L2
nodes.statement: On image classification tasks (CIFAR-10 with ResNet, ImageNet with ResNet), AdamW achieves better test accuracy than Adam with L2 regularization, matching or approaching SGD with momentum performance. The improvement comes from proper regularization that does not interfere with the adaptive learning rate mechanism.
assumptions: Adam update rule as baseline (with L2 regularization in gradient)
AdamW update rule (DP_AW.2) with decoupled weight decay
conclusions: AdamW achieves better generalization than Adam+L2
AdamW closes the gap between Adam and SGD+momentum on image tasks
Hyperparameter tuning is simplified (learning rate and weight decay decouple)

nodes.name: Warm restarts with AdamW (AdamWR)
nodes.statement: Combining AdamW with warm restart learning rate schedules (cosine annealing with restarts) further improves performance. The decoupled weight decay ensures that the regularization effect is consistent across different learning rate phases of the cosine schedule.
assumptions: Cosine annealing with warm restarts schedule
conclusions: Further improved generalization with warm restarts
Consistent regularization across learning rate schedule phases
